title: Identifying independent causal cell types for human diseases and risk variants.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed Zenodo record 10515792 (S-LDSC reference files: sumstats.tgz 2.2 GB, sumstats_indep107.tgz 1.1 GB, many 0.3-1.4 GB LD-score archives) and record 11194201 (one SLDSC_default.zip, 11.3 GB). Listed the GitHub repo ArtemKimUSC/CTFM: data/ and out/ (ctfm, ctfmsnp, SLDSC) contain only .gitignore stubs, no result tables. Europe PMC supplementary-file endpoint timed out once; not retried.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 63 GWAS (genome-wide association studies), 924 cRE (candidate regulatory element) annotations, 79 cell-type sets, 3,091 variant-trait pairs with assigned causal cell types; these result tables are described as Tables S1-S18 but I could not retrieve them.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo inputs are open; the per-variant result tables (supplement) were not retrievable here. Checked file listings only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only candidate label (causal cell type per variant-trait pair) would be the CT-FM-SNP output table; there is no measured label column in the deposited files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Variants are rsIDs/coordinates and cRE annotations as BED-derived LD scores; inputs exist but are genomics-scale archives.

a4_units_stated.note: Posterior inclusion probabilities (0-1) per paper text; not verified in files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper reports 3,091 variant-trait pairs; not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~11.3 GB annotation zip plus 2-3 GB summary statistics
a6_fits_laptop.note: Annotation archive alone is 11.3 GB (seen in Zenodo listing), over the ~5 GB limit.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without the supplement; not a reason for rejection on its own.

a8_label_provenance.note: Causal cell-type assignments and cPIPs (cell-type posterior inclusion probabilities) are outputs of the CT-FM statistical model computed from the same cRE annotations and GWAS data; learning them would distill the model, and using annotations as features would be leakage by construction.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA) would be the natural match, but there is no measured label to fit
backbone.licence: CT-FM code is GPL-3.0 (LICENSE file, 35 kB, seen in repo); Zenodo licence not checked

integration.partner_dataset: AlphaGenome variant-effect predictions or GTEx fine-mapped eQTLs
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether sequence-based regulatory predictions agree with statistically inferred causal cell types; not pursued because both sides are model outputs.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here would only claim to reproduce CT-FM-SNP's cell-type assignments, not true causal cell types.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around a disease-linked genetic variant to predict which cell type it acts through.
plain_idea.train_on: About 3,091 variant-trait pairs (paper's figure, not verified), each with the variant's surrounding DNA and regulatory annotations.
plain_idea.predict: The cell type assigned to each variant, which comes from the authors' own statistical fine-mapping method, not from an experiment.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Geneticists would like to know where a risk variant acts without running cell-type-specific experiments, but here the answer key is itself a model's guess.

ml_idea: Predict CT-FM-SNP causal cell-type assignment from variant sequence with a frozen DNA model; rejected because the label is CT-FM's own output derived from the cRE annotations.

effort.compute_note: Sizes from Zenodo listings only; nothing downloaded or timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Confirm whether any experimentally measured cell-type-of-action label (e.g. MPRA or CRISPR per cell type) exists for these variants; none is in the deposit.

verdict_reason: Statistical-genetics methods paper: the only per-variant label is CT-FM's own posterior output (A8 circular, A2 no measured label), and the deposited inputs are an 11.3 GB annotation archive plus multi-GB summary statistics (A6).
